updated=2026-11-19T13:29:21Z\r\nbody=## Summary  D-owned **offline test** implementation batch for O4 Stage 2 (Member D). Shared production wiring is **Member C's**; this PR does not edit shared files.  This is a **Draft, WIP** PR. It does **not** claim Stage 2 code/CI/acceptance/merge.  ### Baselines - Actual main baseline: `5cdd7589cc73817133a7ca73cf768fc02d0cd19a` - Branch: `feature/o4-stage2-tests` (from `5cdd758`) - Approved contract baseline: `6275725` (v0.6 plans)  ### Approvals referenced (original evidence) - C shared interface �� comment `7008779473` (bound `6275725`) - F pre-impl test design �� review `5974514410` - A pre-impl execution scope �� review `5973684411` (also the D9 pre-code execution-plan approval per A's review) - Record: `docs/test-approvals/O4-Stage2-Evidence-Gate.md`  ### This batch 1. Readiness note (`docs/req/O4-Stage2-Implementation-Readiness-Note.md`) �� D9 pre-work info. 2. T-16 pure-checker benchmark (`test_evidence_gate_benchmark.py`): `check_evidence()` only; fixed 4-report fixture; 5 warmups + 30 measured; nearest-rank p95; **��10 ms diagnostic/non-blocking**; correctness + fixed counts + offline enforceable. 3. T-20 compatibility helpers (independent parts only): `record_decision` signature + `None` return preserved; Stage 1 behavior + historical-state readability. 4. Deterministic fixtures: complete / missing / Market+News `not_required` / N/A-unavailable / original REVIEW / pre-Gate original-rating provenance.  ### Scope / non-goals - **D-owned:** `test/offline/*` O4 tests + fixtures; optional additive pure helper **only if A/C permit**. - **C-owned (not touched):** `trading_graph.py`, `state.py`, `cli/run.py`, `reporting.py`, `report_html.py`, `memory/log.py`. - No `cli/display.py`, no new files beyond the six, no public API change, no automatic CLI retry. - No invented Guard/GateResult API; no fake production seams. - Mandatory **integration** tests needing C's shared wiring remain prepared/not-executed (no skip/xfail masking).  ### Outstanding (coordination) - **O6/C CLI joint-verification evidence** not yet recorded �� blocks C's `cli/run.py` integration. - Runtime observation seam pending C; lifecycle/real-CLI tests target it once confirmed.  _Draft; not for merge._ \r\n--- issue comments (mentions/next) ---\r\n=== PR #25 ===\r\ntitle=feat(o4): run the evidence Gate at the completion boundary user=EloimEssiam draft=False head=feea2e0320aece0504045f1e7cb2b8f3e8e41944 base=e83c3dd75c22eb652425df7dc7ec445d33d4364c updated=2026-11-20T09:34:26Z\r\nbody=## What this changes  Implements C's side of the O4 Stage 2 evidence Gate, per the v0.6 plans in #17.  **Stacked on #23** (`feat/o2-stage2-cli-manifest`), because the approved contract requires preserving O2's pre-run directory reservation and the single post-analysis manifest write in `cli/run.py`. #23 is green and unmerged; this PR should be retargeted to `main` once #23 lands.  ### Files changed  | File | Change | |---|---| | `tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py` | `CompletionRecord`, `record_decision` Gate, `begin_checkpoint`/`end_checkpoint` reset, `last_completion` | | `tradingagents/agents/state.py` | `effective_rating`, `original_rating` | | `cli/run.py` | PM decision held back until the Gate, then published (labelled unapproved on REVIEW) |  `tradingagents/reporting.py`, `tradingagents/report_html.py` and `tradingagents/memory/log.py` need **no change**: each reads the rating through `run_rating()`, and since the Gate sets `final_rating = effective_rating` they inherit the gated value. That is the minimal-change reading of the six-file scope.  ### Runtime contract as implemented  - **`begin_checkpoint()`** clears the record **before** the   `checkpoint_enabled` early return, so it always applies. A new run or a   Resume of the same ticker/date on the same instance is judged afresh ��   no dependence on it being a new process. - **`end_checkpoint()`** clears the record; the observation window closes there. - **`last_completion`** is a read-only property returning `CompletionRecord`   (`gate`, `original_rating`, `published`). Valid from the end of the Gate   until `end_checkpoint`; `None` otherwise. In-memory only, never persisted. - **`record_decision()`**: first call captures the pre-Gate rating, judges once,   publishes. A repeat within the same execution **reuses** `record.gate` and   the originally captured `original_rating` �� it never re-judges and never   re-reads `final_rating` (which the Gate already downgraded). After   persistence completes, a further call returns immediately. - Order is Gate �� `_log_state` �� `store_decision`. - A `json` state-log failure raises as before; the CLI then never reaches   manifest finalisation.  ### Compatibility  A direct `record_decision()` call made **outside** a run's execution window (no `begin_checkpoint`) keeps the pre-Gate behaviour, so existing library callers and the merged regression tests are unaffected. This is why the T-20 merged tests stay green rather than being edited.  ### Not in this PR  - No change to `evidence_gate.py` (Stage 1, D-owned). - No public API change: `record_decision` keeps its signature and `None` return. - No CLI automatic retry. - D's tests (#24) are not included; D owns them.  ## Test results (local, project venv)  | Suite | Command | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | Full suite | `pytest -q` | **1577 passed, 6 skipped**, 1 deselected | | O2 targets | `pytest test/offline/test_o2_manifest.py test/offline/test_o2_cli_manifest.py -q` | **30 passed** | | Memory/CLI/portfolio | `pytest tests/test_cli_memory_log.py tests/test_memory_log.py tests/test_portfolio_context.py -q` | **146 passed** | | Ruff | `ruff check` on the three changed files | All checks passed |  The 6 skips are pre-existing and environmental (POSIX file modes, `langchain_aws` absent, POSIX shell upgrade commands).  **These are local results; CI status is reported separately on this page.**  ## For D  Observation API to target:  ```python graph.begin_checkpoint(ticker, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)   # starts an execution graph.record_decision(ticker, trade_date, final_state)              # Gate runs here rec = graph.last_completion      # CompletionRecord | None rec.gate                 # GateResult: verdict, effective_rating, items, reason, error_kind rec.original_rating      # first pre-Gate rating rec.published            # True once state log AND memory entry are written graph.end_checkpoint()   # clears the record ```  Read `last_completion` **between** `record_decision` returning and `end_checkpoint()`. ## Proposal: pre-code test approval + required-check policy

### Current basis

- Current `main`: `48d75c38177ea30ab48d33112aaa812a0499ea63`
- Current CI jobs: [`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](https://github.com/Caicys297/TradingAgents-CS5351/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml) — `tests (py3.11–3.14 + non-UTC)`, `clean-install smoke`, `ruff (strict, full repo)`
- Existing approval record format: [`docs/test-approvals/TEMPLATE.md`](https://github.com/Caicys297/TradingAgents-CS5351/blob/main/docs/test-approvals/TEMPLATE.md)
- Verified example: [`docs/test-approvals/O4-Evidence-Gate.md`](https://github.com/Caicys297/TradingAgents-CS5351/blob/main/docs/test-approvals/O4-Evidence-Gate.md)
- Reviewer assignment basis: [`docs/req/A-Requirements-Decisions.md`](https://github.com/Caicys297/TradingAgents-CS5351/blob/main/docs/req/A-Requirements-Decisions.md) — F reviews O1/O3/O4/O5; A reviews O2/O6; A reviews execution plans; F owns the six D7 CI gates.
- Schema gate implementation is still unmerged in [PR #30](https://github.com/Caicys297/TradingAgents-CS5351/pull/30), head `e085bfd`, based on `99612ca`, **11/11 checks green**, no approval, enforcement unverified.

### 1. What counts as valid pre-code test approval

A valid approval must be a durable GitHub record — preferably an `APPROVED` review, or an explicit approval comment — containing:

- **Approver:** the reviewer assigned to that scope; normally **F for test plan/CI** and **A for execution/implementation scope**. Where the approved plan assigns A as test reviewer for O2/O6, A’s explicit test-scope approval is required.
- **Exact plan identity:** file path(s), version, and immutable commit SHA. Example: F approved PR #18 at [`aa9fda6` review 5972069186](https://github.com/Caicys297/TradingAgents-CS5351/pull/18#pullrequestreview-5972069186), not merely “latest plan.”
- **Scope:** requirement IDs, test IDs, fixtures, expected results, negative/boundary cases, allowed files, exclusions, and offline command.
- **Timestamp:** GitHub UTC timestamp.
- **Durability:** PR review/comment URL; a `docs/test-approvals/` record is an index, not a substitute for the GitHub record.
- **No retroactive approval:** later PR approval or CI cannot approve a plan retroactively, per the template.

### 2. How implementation PRs link approval and tested SHA

Implementation PR body must include:

- Link to the exact approval review/comment.
- Plan file/version and approved plan SHA.
- Approved requirement/test IDs and any exclusions.
- The **tested commit SHA**.
- Exact test commands and CI run URL for that SHA.
- A statement that code review/PR approval is separate from pre-code test approval.

If the branch is rebased or amended, update the tested SHA and rerun CI. CI on an older SHA does not validate the merge candidate.

### 3. CI results vs human approval

- Human approval defines the agreed test scope and expected behavior.
- CI proves the tested commit passed the configured automated checks.
- A green CI run **does not** grant or renew test-plan approval.
- A human approval does not prove the code passes; both are required.
- PR review approval is a separate code-review step, not a pre-code test approval.

### 4. Evidence required before a check becomes required

Before requiring a GitHub status check:

1. Check exists in the main workflow and has a stable check-run name.
2. It is deterministic/offline and runs on `pull_request` and `push` to `main`.
3. It passes on a PR based on current `main`.
4. Failure mode is actionable and documented.
5. F confirms test/CI behavior; A confirms branch-protection/enforcement.
6. A/admin records the exact required-check list and any bypass policy.
7. A blocked-merge trial proves the check actually blocks merging.

**Rollout recommendation:** initially require the existing checks only — `tests (py3.11)`, `tests (py3.12, America/New_York)`, `tests (py3.13)`, `tests (py3.14)`, `clean-install smoke`, and `ruff (strict, full repo)`. Add `requirements schema` only after PR #30 is approved, rebased to main, and merged. Do not require the AI-use, type, dependency, or semantic checks until A/F separately approve them. This avoids adding gates beyond the agreed scope.

### 5. Revisions

| Revision type | Approval treatment |
|---|---|
| Typo, formatting, comment, or wording with no change to test IDs, assertions, expected results, allowed files, or public interfaces | Record an addendum/comment at the new SHA linking the original approval and confirming no scope change. F/A should explicitly acknowledge; no full reapproval unless they require it. |
| New/removed/changed test IDs, expected outputs, fixtures, allowed files, execution scope, or public interfaces | **New approval required at the new plan SHA before code changes.** Prior approval is not reusable. |
| Within-scope implementation change that does not alter the approved test contract | No new plan approval, but PR review and CI must cover the tested SHA. |

Historical examples support this: F requested corrections on `07685bb` and then approved the corrected `aa9fda6` ([5971943257](https://github.com/Caicys297/TradingAgents-CS5351/pull/18#pullrequestreview-5971943257), [5972069186](https://github.com/Caicys297/TradingAgents-CS5351/pull/18#pullrequestreview-5972069186)); O4 approvals on `6275725` do not automatically cover later head `8be0c0f`; O5’s F approval is tied to `e68b25c`.

### 6. Lightweight blocked-merge trial

After A enables **one** required check on `main`:

1. Create a throwaway branch/PR from current `main` with a deliberate failure for that check.
2. Let the required check fail; record the PR URL and failing check URL.
3. Attempt merge; confirm GitHub blocks it and capture `mergeable_state=blocked` or the equivalent branch-protection/UI evidence.
4. Close the trial PR **without merging**; delete the branch.
5. Optionally push a passing commit to show the same check turns green, then close.

This proves enforcement without changing production code or requiring all six gates.

- [`scripts/validate_requirements.py` on PR #30](https://github.com/Caicys297/TradingAgents-CS5351/blob/e085bfd9699375345f914327fe584e1d27bde4c8/scripts/validate_requirements.py)

A `docs/test-approvals/` record indexes it but does not replace it. Later PR approval/CI cannot retroactively approve a plan.
> 2. **Implementation PR:** link the approval URL, plan SHA/version, scope, tested commit SHA, exact commands, and CI run for that SHA. Update the tested SHA after any rebase/amend.

None if unresolvable.\"\"\"\r\n    try:\r\n        proc = subprocess.run(\r\n            [\"git\", \"-C\", str(root), \"rev-parse\", \"--verify\", f\"origin/{base_ref}^{{commit}}\"],\r\n            capture_output=True, text=True,\r\n        )\r\n    except FileNotFoundError:\r\n        return None\r\n    if proc.returncode != 0:\r\n        return None\r\n    return proc.stdout.strip()\r\n\r\n\r\ndef _is_ancestor(ancestor: str, descendant: str, root: Path) -> bool:\r\n    try:\r\n        proc = subprocess.run(\r\n            [\"git\", \"-C\", str(root), \"merge-base\", \"--is-ancestor\", ancestor, descendant],\r\n            capture_output=True, text=True,\r\n        )\r\n    except FileNotFoundError:\r\n        return False\r\n    return proc.returncode == 0\r\n\r\n\r\ndef _commit_in_range(sha: str, base_ref: str, root: Path) -> bool:\r\n    \"\"\"Whether ``sha`` is in the *actual PR history*: reachable from the reviewed\r\n    head AND NOT already reachable from the verified base commit.\r\n\r\n    This excludes baseline/main commits (already on origin/<base>) and unrelated\r\n    SHAs, and is robust to GitHub's synthetic merge checkout: we test ancestry\r\n    against the real ``origin/<base>`` base, not the workflow merge commit.\r\n    \"\"\"\r\n    if not _commit_exists(sha, root):\r\n        return False\r\n    if not _is_ancestor(sha, \"HEAD\", root):\r\n        return False  # not in the reviewed head's history\r\n    base_sha = _resolve_base_commit(base_ref, root)\r\n    if base_sha is None:\r\n        return False  # cannot verify exclusion from base -> reject\r\n    # Exclude commits already reachable from base (not this PR's work).\r\n    return not _is_ancestor(sha, base_sha, root)\r\n\r\n\r\ndef _json_has_transcript_content(path: Path) -> bool:\r\n    \"\"\"A JSON export is genuine evidence only if it carries real conversation\r\n    content: an OpenCode-style object with a non-empty ``messages`` array whose\r\n    entries have ``parts``, OR any structure with substantive text. Empty ``{}``,\r\n    metadata-only records, and bare provenance stubs are rejected.\"\"\"\r\n    import json as _json\r\n\r\n    try:\r\n        data = _json.loads(path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\"))\r\n    except (OSError, ValueError):\r\n        return False\r\n    if not isinstance(data, dict) or not data:\r\n        return False  # {}, non-dict, empty\r\n    messages = data.get(\"messages\")\r\n    if isinstance(messages, list) and messages:\r\n        # require at least one message entry that actually has parts/content\r\n        for m in messages:\r\n            if isinstance(m, dict) and isinstance(m.get(\"parts\"), list) and m[\"parts\"]:\r\n                return True\r\n        return False\r\n    # Metadata-only records (e.g. a provenance stub) -> reject: any of these\r\n    # summary markers without a real ``messages`` array is not transcript content.\r\n    meta_markers = {\"full_export_sha256\", \"message_count\", \"role_counts\", \"source\", \"note\", \"session_id\"}\r\n    if set(data.keys()) & meta_markers:\r\n        return False\r\n    # Otherwise require an OpenCode-style shape with messages+parts.\r\n    return False\r\n\r\n\r\ndef _is_genuine_export(path: Path) -> bool:\r\n    \"\"\"Resolvable reference counts as export evidence only if it is real transcript\r\n    content: a JSON export carrying messages/parts, or a non-summary transcript file\r\n    that does not self-identify as an authored summary. ``{}``, metadata-only\r\n    records, and authored summaries are rejected.\"\"\"\r\n    if not path.is_file():\r\n        return False\r\n    if path.suffix.lower() in (\".json\", \".jsonl\"):\r\n        return _json_has_transcript_content(path)\r\n    try:\r\n        head = path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")[:2000].lower()\r\n    except OSError:\r\n        return False\r\n    is_summary = (\"not a raw\" in head) or (\"authored\" in head and \"summary\" in head)\r\n    return not is_summary\r\n\r\n\r\ndef _validate_entry(text_lines: list[str], root: Path, base_ref: str, check_commits: bool = True) -> list[str]:\r\n    joined = \"\\n\".join(text_lines)\r\n    if not joined.strip():\r\n        return [\"no added content (whitespace-only or unchanged entry) �?not valid evidence\"]\r\n\r\n    lowered = joined.lower()\r\n    missing = [lbl for lbl in REQUIRED_FIELD_LABELS if lbl not in lowered]\r\n    if missing:\r\n        return [f\"missing field label(s): {', '.join(missing)}\"]\r\n\r\n    problems: list[str] = []\r\n\r\n    # Genuine session/export reference: a non-PR https URL whose path denotes a\r\n    # session/export, or a resolvable transcripts/ export file.\r\n    session_urls = [u for u in HTTPS_URL_RE.findall(joined) if _is_session_url(u)]\r\n    transcript_refs = list(TRANSCRIPT_REF_RE.findall(joined))\r\n    resolvable_exports = [r for r in transcript_refs if _is_genuine_export(root / r)]\r\n\r\n    if not session_urls and not resolvable_exports:\r\n        if PR_URL_RE.search(joined):\r\n            problems.append(\r\n                \"PR URL is not session evidence (query/fragment containing 'session' does \"\r\n                \"not count; need a genuine session/export URL path or a resolvable export file)\"\r\n            )\r\n        else:\r\n            problems.append(\r\n                \"no genuine session/export reference (need an https session/export URL or a \"\r\n                \"resolvable transcripts/ export file)\"\r\n            )\r\n\r\n    if ABS_PATH_RE.search(joined):\r\n        problems.append(\"evidence references a machine-specific absolute path (reviewers cannot access it)\")\r\n\r\n    # Implementation-commit association must be a REAL commit in this PR's range.\r\n    if base_ref and check_commits:\r\n        shas = COMMIT_SHA_RE.findall(joined)\r\n        real = [s for s in shas if _commit_exists(s, root)]\r\n\r\n\r\n"
}
